issues.description: reload() silently breaks the UrlMarkManager invariant when the file fails to parse mid-reload
issues.detail: The contract of reload() should be: postcondition leaves marks in a consistent state matching disk, OR raises and leaves the prior state untouched. Current implementation clears marks first, then parses; if _parse_line raises (InvalidUrlError, etc.), the manager is left half-populated and emits changed. Either parse-then-swap, or document the partial-failure contract.

issues.description: Command names and feature-file scenarios disagree with the established quickmark-/bookmark- naming contract
issues.detail: Every other command in this module uses singular hyphenated form: quickmark-save, quickmark-add, bookmark-add, bookmark-load. The new commands are quickmarks_reload / bookmarks_reload (plural, and the BDD steps use quickmarks-reload). This breaks the implicit naming contract callers rely on for discoverability and is inconsistent within the same file. Pick quickmark-reload / bookmark-reload.

issues.description: changed signal now fires from __init__ via reload(), altering the construction-time contract
issues.detail: Previously the constructor populated marks without emitting changed; now __init__ calls reload() which emits changed.emit() during construction. Any subscriber connected before/at construction (or any future code assuming changed means a post-init mutation) will see a spurious initial event. The signal's implicit contract — fired on user-visible mutation — is weakened.

issues.description: Two BDD scenarios share an empty Scenario: title, hurting traceability
issues.detail: Both new scenarios are declared as bare `Scenario:` with no name. Test names are part of the spec — they tell future maintainers what behavior is being asserted. Name them e.g. `Scenario: Reloading bookmarks from disk`.

issues.description: Unit test does not cover the contract it most needs to: removal and replacement semantics
issues.detail: test_reload only verifies replacement of one entry by another. The interesting postconditions of reload() — entries removed from disk disappear from marks, added entries appear, ordering reflects disk — are not asserted. A test with multiple entries before and a disjoint set after would pin the contract.

issues.description: reload() docstring conflates two subtypes and omits pre/postconditions
issues.detail: The method lives on UrlMarkManager (supertype) but the docstring says 'Reload quickmarks/bookmarks from disk', which is implementation-leak language. State the supertype contract: 'Discard current marks and repopulate from the backing file; emits changed on completion.' Subtypes inherit it unchanged — that is the LSP win.

review.summary: The change adds a useful reload operation, but the abstract data type's contract is under-specified and the implementation weakens two invariants. First, reload() clears state before parsing, so a parse error leaves the manager in a half-populated state with a changed signal already in flight — the postcondition of "marks matches disk OR unchanged" is not preserved. Second, routing __init__ through reload() changes the construction-time contract by emitting changed during init. Finally, the new command names (quickmarks_reload / bookmarks_reload) break the singular quickmark-/bookmark- naming pattern used by every sibling command, which is itself a small contract callers depend on. Tighten the spec, parse-then-swap, and align the names.
